orca-dl.checkpoint: seed_1 .. seed_8 (one checkpoint per training seed)
orca-dl.code_source: https://github.com/OpenEarthLab/ORCA-DL (official PyTorch; native dependency-light port in weatherai/models/orca_dl)
orca-dl.code_licence: official repo: no LICENSE file (all rights reserved by default); this port: MIT
orca-dl.weights_source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/JayKuo/ORCA-DL-data (model_weights/seed_{1..8}.bin, stat/{mean,std}/*.npy); mirror: OneDrive link in the official README
orca-dl.weights_licence: not stated (HF dataset card has no licence); Zenodo 15383228 (CC-BY-4.0) covers data only

inputs.name: tos
inputs.long_name: sea surface temperature of the model's top layer (CMIP6 tos during training)
inputs.source_name: sst in the official GODAS example = GODAS 5 m potential temperature
inputs.notes: With GODAS initial conditions this is a near-surface water temperature PROXY (5 m), not a satellite/bulk SST.

inputs.name: tauu
inputs.long_name: eastward surface wind stress on the ocean (positive eastward)
inputs.notes: Official example: equatorial-Pacific January mean -0.047 N/m^2 (easterly trades -> negative).

inputs.name: tauv
inputs.long_name: northward surface wind stress on the ocean

orca-dl.history: 1 monthly-mean state (the initial month); wind stress of the initial month only
orca-dl.grid: regular 1 deg, lat -63.5..63.5 (128, south->north), lon 0.5..359.5 (360); official preprocessing: cdo remapbil
orca-dl.vertical: 16 depth levels 10,15,30,50,75,100,125,150,200,250,300,400,500,600,800,1000 m; official preprocessing: cdo intlevel (linear, no extrapolation)
orca-dl.normalisation: x_n = (x - mean[m]) / std[m] per grid point and level, m = calendar month of the field (0 = January); input uses the initial month, lead L is de-normalised with month (m0 + L) % 12 (official demo.ipynb); NaN -> 0 after normalisation (official)

outputs.name: tos
outputs.long_name: sea surface temperature of the model's top layer (CMIP6 tos during training)
outputs.source_name: sst in the official GODAS example = GODAS 5 m potential temperature
outputs.notes: With GODAS initial conditions this is a near-surface water temperature PROXY (5 m), not a satellite/bulk SST.

orca-dl.time_semantics: lead L = monthly mean of calendar month (init month + L); the init month is the monthly mean used as input

forcings.name: tauu, tauv
forcings.notes: the model has no future-forcing input: wind stress is encoded once from the initial month

orca-dl.spatial_mask: ocean points where the GODAS input is defined (per variable; ~31-34 % of the 128x360 domain is NaN); domain stops at 63.5S/63.5N -> no Arctic, no Southern Ocean poleward of 63.5S; outputs are masked to NaN outside the input-valid mask, never zero-filled
orca-dl.ensemble: no stochastic sampling; members = different training seeds (seed_1..8) of the same model. Official predict.py averages the seeds' normalised outputs. Seeds are NOT independent models.

technical_max_lead.reason: autoregressive: lead-time experts for 1..6, the lead-6 prediction is fed back; official predict.sh uses 24 months; no hard limit in code

validated_lead.reason: no independent multi-init hindcast run by WeatherAI

implemented.detail: native PyTorch port; parameter names follow the official module

weights_obtainable.detail: HF dataset (seeds 1-8) + OneDrive; download with weatherai.models.orca_dl.download

real_data_inference.detail: one GODAS initial state (Jan 1980, official example), seed_1, 11 leads, CPU and HF GPU; SST_S2S reported a monthly inference with the official checkpoint (external)

official_parity.detail: 7 monthly steps vs official modules, seed_1, rel. L2 <= 7.3e-7

multi_init_long_rollout.detail: seeds 2-8, other initial months/years and >11-month rollouts not run

independent_hindcast.detail: no hindcast skill computed by WeatherAI

orca-dl.paper: Guo et al., Sci. Adv. 11, eadu2488 (2025)
orca-dl.paper_claims: seasonal-to-decadal ocean prediction skill reported in the paper (not reproduced here)
orca-dl.resources: GPU: 2.4 GB peak, 7 steps 0.82 s (HF ZeroGPU); CPU fp32 feasible (~2.2 GB weights per seed)
limitations: GODAS 'sst' is 5 m potential temperature: SST proxy, keep separate from OISST/ERA5 SST
wind stress held at the initial month
GODAS raw uflx/vflx sign convention not re-checked against PSL files here (PSL unreachable); the official example is eastward-positive

fuxi-s2s.code_source: https://github.com/tpys/FuXi-S2S (official ONNX driver inference.py / data_util.py); native PyTorch port in weatherai/models/fuxi_s2s (secondary backend)
fuxi-s2s.code_licence: official driver: see upstream repo; this port: MIT

inputs.name: sst
inputs.long_name: ERA5 sea surface temperature (NaN over land, official mask.nc)

inputs.name: ttr
inputs.long_name: top net thermal radiation as a mean flux
inputs.notes: official input builder: ERA5 hourly accumulation [J/m^2] / 3600

inputs.name: tp
inputs.long_name: precipitation, daily mean of ERA5 hourly accumulations, x1000, clipped to [0, 1000]

fuxi-s2s.history: 2 consecutive daily means (init day - 1, init day), 76 channels, order = weatherai.models.fuxi_s2s.CHANNELS
fuxi-s2s.grid: regular 1.5 deg incl. poles, lat 90..-90 (121, north->south), lon 0..358.5 (240)
fuxi-s2s.normalisation: inside the ONNX graph (mean/std initialisers); NaN -> 0; precipitation input channel zeroed by the graph

outputs.name: sst
outputs.long_name: ERA5 sea surface temperature (NaN over land, official mask.nc)

outputs.name: ttr
outputs.long_name: top net thermal radiation as a mean flux
outputs.notes: official input builder: ERA5 hourly accumulation [J/m^2] / 3600

outputs.name: tp
outputs.long_name: precipitation, daily mean of ERA5 hourly accumulations, x1000, clipped to [0, 1000]

fuxi-s2s.time_semantics: ERA5 daily means; input times = [init-1d, init]; output of step k (0-based) = daily mean of init + (k+1) days
fuxi-s2s.spatial_mask: sst NaN over land in the input (official land_to_nan with data/mask.nc); WeatherAI re-applies the input land mask to the sst output (the network writes values everywhere)
fuxi-s2s.ensemble: stochastic latent: two Gaussian draws per step (RandomNormalLike in the ONNX). Official README example: 11 members. WeatherAI default replaces the two draws by graph inputs with seeded noise rng([seed, member, step]) (identical to the internal sampling in distribution, reproducible, shared with the native backend).

technical_max_lead.reason: lead-time encoding trained for step 0..41; official total_step = 42; refused beyond

implemented.detail: ONNX runner (official graph) + native PyTorch port

real_data_inference.detail: official ERA5 sample (2020-06-01/02): native fp32 1 step + 3-step chain on CPU, 1 step on HF GPU; SST_S2S reported 11 members x 42 days with the official ONNX (external)

official_parity.detail: native fp32 vs onnxruntime fp16 graph, same injected noise: step-0 rel. L2 6.3e-6, 3-step chain <= 1.4e-5 (worst channel 1.2e-3); not bitwise (fp16 vs fp32)

multi_init_long_rollout.detail: 42-day x 11-member ONNX run reported by SST_S2S; not run from this repo

independent_hindcast.detail: no S2S skill (RPSS/CRPS/ACC) computed by WeatherAI

fuxi-s2s.paper_claims: paper reports S2S skill over 42 days (weeks 3-6) against ECMWF S2S; not reproduced here
fuxi-s2s.resources: native fp32: 5.4 GB GPU peak, 0.67 s/step (HF ZeroGPU); ~25 s/step on 8 CPU cores; ONNX fp16 graph on CPU similar
limitations: CC-BY-NC-ND: non-commercial, no derivatives of the weights; outputs must not be presented as an official product
the native port is a secondary backend verified for 1 step + 3-step chain only
official ONNX samples noise without a seed; reproducibility needs the WeatherAI noise injection

ace2.code_source: https://github.com/ai2cm/ace (fme, Apache-2.0); native SFNO + stepper in weatherai/models/ace2

inputs.name: <44 in_names from the checkpoint>
inputs.long_name: prognostic state (8 hybrid-sigma layers + surface) and forcings; names read from stepper.config.in_names at load time

ace2.vertical: 8 hybrid sigma-pressure layers (ak, bk in the checkpoint)
ace2.normalisation: per-variable scalar mean/std from the checkpoint (stepper.normalizer)

outputs.name: <50 out_names from the checkpoint>
outputs.long_name: includes PRATEsfc [kg m-2 s-1], TMP2m, surface fluxes

ace2.time_semantics: instantaneous state every 6 h; fluxes/precipitation are 6-h means
ace2.spatial_mask: global; SST taken from the forcing wherever round(ocean_fraction) == 1
ace2.ensemble: deterministic network; ensembles need IC/forcing perturbations (not implemented)

technical_max_lead.reason: no code limit; multi-year runs are the design target of the paper

real_data_inference.detail: 2020-06-01 IC, 32 steps (8 days), CPU + HF GPU

official_parity.detail: rollout vs fme, 12 steps, max rel. error 7.9e-5

ace2.paper: Watt-Meyer et al., npj Clim. Atmos. Sci. 8, 205 (2025)
ace2.resources: 3.1 GB GPU peak, 32 steps 3.5 s (HF ZeroGPU)
limitations: atmosphere-only: SST and sea ice are inputs, so a run is an atmospheric response to the given SST, NOT an SST forecast
with observed future SST the run is a conditional hindcast, not a forecast

neuralgcm.code_source: https://github.com/neuralgcm/neuralgcm (official JAX) + dinosaur dycore; weatherai wraps it unchanged
files: <name>.pkl (58 MB for 2.8 deg ... ~1 GB for 0.7 deg)

inputs.name: <model.input_variables>
inputs.long_name: geopotential, temperature, u, v, specific humidity, cloud water/ice on 37 pressure levels

neuralgcm.grid: Gaussian grid of the checkpoint (2.8 deg: 128x64)
neuralgcm.vertical: 37 pressure levels in, sigma levels inside
neuralgcm.time_step: internal 1 h (2.8 deg) ... ; output every requested timedelta

forcings.name: sea_surface_temperature
forcings.notes: WeatherAI policy must be chosen: persist_initial or provided

neuralgcm.ensemble: stochastic checkpoints: seed -> member; deterministic checkpoints: one member

technical_max_lead.reason: no code limit; forcings beyond the given series are held per policy

validated_lead.reason: WeatherAI: demo snapshot + one 24-h precipitation case

implemented.detail: official JAX path wrapped (forecast backend); the native PyTorch port is PARTIAL (learned components + spherical harmonics, no dycore) and is NOT offered as a forecaster

real_data_inference.detail: precip checkpoints 24 h from 2020-01-01 vs ERA5 (2026-10-02); NeuralGCMForecaster (official JAX, deterministic_2_8_deg, CPU) on the official demo ERA5 snapshot 1959-01-02, 4 x 6 h, 185 s incl. compile, peak RSS 2.6 GB (2026-10-08). Lead 0 (decoded initial state) is not the analysis: 157 K at 10 hPa vs input minimum 183 K

official_parity.detail: forecast path IS the official code (wrapper only converts I/O)

limitations: atmosphere-only: SST/sea ice prescribed (persisted or given) -> not an SST forecast
partial PyTorch port must not be used for forecasts

unicm.weights_source: none: README expects a locally trained runs/SaveModel (20 seeds trained on CMIP6 CESM2-FV2 + reanalyses)

inputs.name: 5 channels
inputs.long_name: upper-ocean / atmosphere anomaly fields on a 12x72 grid (see official LoadData.py)

implemented.detail: architecture bit-exact vs official code with RANDOM weights

weights_obtainable.detail: official GitHub HEAD 67fe4c1 contains no checkpoint and no link (re-checked 2026-10-08); Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19173780 is code-only and HF had no checkpoint (checked 2026-10-01; Zenodo/HF unreachable from this environment on 2026-10-08)

real_data_inference.detail: impossible without weights; random-weight outputs are never forecasts

unicm.paper: Yuan et al., Nat. Mach. Intell. 8, 930-941 (2026)
limitations: retraining = separate project: CMIP6 + ORAS5/ERA5/GODAS/SODA data, ~20 seeds, explicit train/validation/test years
